statement: Intradermal avotermin (recombinant human TGF-β3) given before and 24 h after wounding improved visual scar scores at 6 and 12 months versus placebo in three double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-participant phase I/II studies in healthy volunteers.

context.model: 1 cm full-thickness incisions in healthy volunteers
context.intervention: avotermin 0.25–500 ng/100 µL per linear cm, two doses
context.comparator: placebo or standard care, within participant

measurement.assay: blinded visual scar assessment (VAS); total scar score
measurement.effect: median VAS improvement 5 mm at 6 months and 8 mm at 12 months at 50 ng; dose-dependent total-score improvement in the third study

replication.note: Sponsor-run (Renovo). The later phase II (McCollum 2011) is the same sponsor.

drift: The sponsor reported in 2011 that the phase 3 programme failed; no peer-reviewed publication of the phase 3 was located as of 2026-09-11, so the published record still reads as a success.
limitations: small effect sizes on a visual scale

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (PubMed) and Crossref metadata, checked 2026-09-11; no source opened at figure level
